runs.question: What two information security risks does the NIST Generative AI Profile describe, and how does NIST AI 100-2 describe indirect prompt injection?

answer.text:
The passages don't support a full answer to either part.

**Part 1: Two information security risks in the NIST Generative AI Profile (AI 600-1).** The retrieved passages from AI 600-1 are only its cover page and title page (pages 1–2). They contain no content on information security risks, so I can't name the two risks from this evidence. One other document notes that the profile highlights twelve different categories of risk from generative AI in more detail, but the passages don't list them.

**Part 2: How NIST AI 100-2 describes indirect prompt injection.** The retrieved pages give no definition or description of the attack. They show only where it appears in the taxonomy. Indirect Prompt Injection has the ID NISTAML.015, and it is listed under Privacy Compromises (ID: NISTAML.03). The same listing shows that Indirect Prompt Injection (ID: NISTAML.015) also appears in an earlier category whose heading is not visible in the passage. The bibliography also cites "Data exfiltration from writer.com with indirect prompt injection, 2023", but it doesn't explain the attack.

The report does say its attacks are classified by AI system type, ML life cycle stage, attacker goals and objectives, attacker capabilities and access, and attacker knowledge of the learning process and beyond. That is the general framework, not a description of this specific attack.

The pages containing the Generative AI Profile's risk descriptions and AI 100-2's indirect prompt injection definition would be needed to answer fully.
